Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  June 1, 2023

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on June 1, 2023. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Jacob Fragoso- District 2,
  Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3, Commissioner
  Christopher Beck - District 4

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Sabrina Barnes  Director
  Craig Civitello  Park Maintenance Lead Worker
  Bharat Devlia  Food Services Manager
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant
  Mary Rosounet-Rouzan  Recreation Supervisor

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. None

STAFF REPORTS. Staff presented a report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission discuss and recommend the Mayor and Council Members take the following
actions: approve Amendment Thirteen of the Elderly Nutrition Program Contract with Los
Angeles County.

It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner Fragoso that the
Commission hereby approves the recommendation. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:
Ayes: Brown, Fragoso, Denmon, McLemore, and Beck
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORTS - PARKS ADMINISTRATION.

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

The Parks Supervisor, Juan Mata reported: This past month graffiti staff repainted six
baseball bleachers that seat approximately 40 people each as well as back boards for the
Dodger Dreamfield dugouts at Vincent Park. Staff also repainted three activity rooms and
the small kitchen at Darby Park, replaced two broken toilets and two broken sinks at
Rogers Park, and repaired three broken irrigation main lines at Vincent Park. The graffiti
hotline number is (310) 412-8739.

 REPORTS - RECREATION.
The Recreation Supervisor, Anthony Harris, reported the following: The goal of keeping
young people in the Inglewood community moving is alive and well. Since the last
commission meeting, the Inglewood Youth Sports League programs have provided
numerous programs and memorable experiences for kids in the city. The youth basketball
and soccer seasons concluded, the Spring Dodgers Dreamteam season came and went,
and two new Dodgers Dreamfields were unveiled with 400 youth participating in the
ceremony. All the aforementioned programs combined focused on developing sport
specific skills, healthy competition, and enjoyable memories for 585 youth.

The 90-minute youth sports clinics series is in full swing as youngsters get an opportunity
to be introduced to various sports, develop skills, and have fun. Staff recently completed
a tennis clinic for the youth last weekend led by city partner Doris Obih of the 40 Love
Foundation. A sold-out youth soccer clinic will be held this Saturday in collaboration with
partner Jose Palomares of PCSC at Champions Field. These clinics allow us to introduce
new sports like volleyball and lacrosse to the youth which are also being offered this
summer. The chance to explore new sports is important and we are pleased to provide
these opportunities.

With summer upon us, our Dodgers Dreamteam “Summer Season” has now selected
teams for five divisions, with 18 teams, 20 volunteer coaches, and 216 participants. The
Dodgers Dreamteam programs have a combined total of 413 youth in the program for
2023. Practices started this week, uniform distribution is next Saturday, and games will be
played on Mondays (Sr. Softball), Thursdays (Jr. Softball), and Saturdays (Minors, Majors,
and Jr. Baseball). The excitement begins on June 12th. Come on out to the two new Dodgers
Dreamfields at Edward Vincent Jr. or Darby Park to catch the action. The season will run
through the week of August 14th and conclude with picnic style “end of the season” team
parties on August 26th.

For more information regarding Inglewood  Youth  Sports  leagues,  visit:
https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

SUMMER FOOD/ CACFP PROGRAM:

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

The Summer Food Program started on June 12, 2023. The program hours are Monday through
Friday, providing breakfast, lunch and snacks at seven sites.An average of 350 meals are served per
week.

REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES.
The Human Services Supervisor, Bharat Devlia, reported the following: 1)Transportation: Our
Senior and Disabled Transportation Program is continuing to provide trips to critical appointments
such as dialysis and doctors’ appointments as well as leisure trips to locations in and around
Inglewood and Hawthorne. Drivers as well as passengers continue to wear facemasks during
transport. 2) Senior Center Operations: The Inglewood Senior Center started a new Social Media
class that has been well received and filled to capacity. We have another class that starts at the
end of February, A Matter of Balance which is also filled to capacity. The Voice of Experience
monthly newsletter has been re-introduced and we are currently on our third month of providing
the monthly newsletter to our seniors so they can stay informed on Senior Center happenings. To
note, the Senior Center will be closed in recognition of Cesar Chavez Day on March 31, 2023. 3)
Nutrition: We are serving approximately 350 seniors per week through home-delivered meals for
homebound seniors and congregate lunches at our Senior Center. Our Senior Center lunchroom is
set up to accommodate safe social distancing and we look forward to continuing to provide fresh
cooked meals on a daily basis to our seniors. We continue to provide fresh produce weekly in
collaboration with the Social Justice Learning Institute. 4) The Child and Adult Care Food Program
(CACFP) serves meals to youth 18 years old and under and operates at three sites (Crenshaw
Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park). The CACFP is on hold while we contract a food vendor. The
program's hours are Monday 2:30 PM - 3:30 PM and snacks from 4:30 PM - 5:00 PM. We served
an average of 70 meals per day at all three sites. We hope to provide more meals once we have a
new vendor to benefit the youth of our community. 5) We are currently working with the
Inglewood Unified School District (IUSD) to reestablish the After-School Program (ASRP) and will
know in the coming weeks, which schools will participate in the ASRP.

REPORTS - DIRECTOR.
No Report

PUBLIC COMMENTS. Angela Evans (longtime Resident) expressed concerns about the adbsence
of lighting at Darby Park Pickle Ball/Tennis courts. She also mentioned possible parking expansion.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Brown: asked When will the Martin Luther
King Day Planning Committee resume meeting?

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:36 p.m.
